ground_truth.unit: log points of annualised household electricity consumption (kWh)
ground_truth.context: Table 2 ("Effect of the Reform on Residential Electricity Consumption and Expenditure (2011-2014)"), column (1), row Reform (T): the paper's difference-in-differences estimate of the August 2013 Spanish electricity pricing reform (fixed charge raised, regulated volumetric rate cut) on household electricity consumption, estimated by OLS.  Data: Spanish Household Budget Survey households interviewed between August 2011 and April 2014, each interviewed twice, in the same two-week period of two consecutive years; the control group has both interviews before the reform, the treated group its second interview after it.  T is the post-reform dummy for interviews whose electricity bill falls under the reform (the paper places the response one month after the reform, when households receive a reformed bill).  Dependent variable: log of electricity consumption in the month before the interview (kWh, annualised by the survey).  Regressors: T, log household price per kWh (expenditure divided by consumption), log income and its square, months since reform, and controls for household size, number of rooms, dwelling surface, elderly members, education of the household head, household economic situation (number of economically active members), renting, building older than 25 years, municipality-size dummies, urban area, province capital, regional dummies, quarterly dummies and year fixed effects.  No household fixed effects.  Standard errors clustered at the household level.

i4r.notes: Team 49 blanket verdict (code reproduces the paper's output); no meta-database row for column 1.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: LIML is hand-coded as a k-class estimator (the installed ivreg package has no LIML method); household-clustered sandwich SEs with Stata-style small-sample factor.
Household fixed-effects IV is estimated by LIML on within-household demeaned data.

Treatment dummy is the dataset's TT202 (reform dummy accounting for the one-month billing lag, matching Section 3.1's 'second reformed bill'), chosen after comparing the T2-based estimates with the claimed values (attempt-6).
Retirement-income dummy not included as a control (including it drops 73 observations below the reported N = 20,872).
cell.notes: Data: analysis file data_to_run_DOFILE3.dta, 2011-2014 panel (T2 non-missing, 25,775 obs), restricted to complete cases on the regression variables -> N = 20,872, 10,729 households, exactly as in Table 2. Dependent variables lnc_ele / lng_ele (annualised kWh / EUR); price lnPRE (household kWh price deflated by the time price index); income lny, lny^2; controls: months since reform (dist), household size, rooms, surface, elderly, education and economic-situation dummies, renting, building >25 years, municipality-size dummies, urban, province capital, region dummies, quarter dummies, year FE; household FE in cols 3,4,7,8; SEs clustered by household. Instruments: deflated effective prices of potatoes, water and fuel (lnPRE_papas_, lnPRE_aguav_, lnPRE_gascar_, with the dataset's filled values for non-purchasers). Attempt history: 1-2 exploration (columns, sample counts); 3 crashed (ivreg has no LIML) -> hand-coded LIML; 4 full run with T = T2, compared with claims (claim 1); 5 exploration of price/instrument construction; 6 specification grid compared with claims, crashed before printing RESULT lines (claim 2) -> switched to T = TT202; 7 full run, compared with claims (claim 3): all OLS/FE and FE-IV columns match to about 3 decimals, but the pooled LIML column 2 (and less so column 6) does not: my pooled first stage is weak (cluster F ~8 vs the paper's 379.6), so the pooled IV price coefficient is +0.31 instead of -0.94; 8 exploratory first-stage F diagnostics found no principled alternative exogenous set or instrument definition reproducing the paper's strong pooled first stage, so I reverted: the final files are an exact copy of attempt-7 (script unchanged).
